`r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#]*)"`

The tilde `~` is missing from the character set.
I should add `~` to this regex.

Let's read the file around line 101 to be sure.

The line is:
`r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#]*)"`

I will add `~` to the character set.
`r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~]*)"`

Wait, let me check if `~` needs to be escaped or if it's fine in a character class. In Python regex character classes, `~` is just a literal character.

Let's verify this with a small script.

steps.message:
Wait, `Span(6, 30, 'repr.url')`.
The text is `"Visit http://example.com/~user"`.
`V` is 0, `i` is 1, `s` is 2, `i` is 3, `t` is 4, ` ` is 5.
`h` is 6.
`http://example.com/~user`
`h` (6), `t` (7), `t` (8), `p` (9), `:` (10), `/` (11), `/` (12), `e` (13), `x` (14), `a` (15), `m` (16), `p` (17), `l` (18), `e` (19), `.` (20), `c` (21), `o` (22), `m` (23), `/` (24), `~` (25), `u` (26), `s` (27), `e` (28), `r` (29).
So the end index should be 30.
My manual count was wrong. `6 + 24 = 30`.
So `Span(6, 30, 'repr.url')` is exactly what I wanted!

Let's re-run the test with the correct end index.
